weeks.topic: ¿Qué tal el verano? Diagnostic and restaurant vocabulary
objectives: Reactivate Spanish 1A skills in a new context
Name table items and restaurant foods

days.title: Diagnostic
days.work: Hold a 3-minute conversation with a parent about your summer, family, and likes, then take a short 1A diagnostic quiz to find gaps to target.

days.title: Table setting
days.work: Learn 12 table-setting words and set the table while naming each item aloud: Pongo el tenedor a la izquierda.

days.title: Restaurant foods
days.work: Learn main dishes, desserts, and drinks (el bistec, el arroz, el flan) and build a three-course menu.

days.title: Polite requests
days.work: Learn me trae..., ¿me puede traer...?, ¿algo más?, la cuenta por favor and practice with a parent as camarero.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a restaurant vocabulary quiz and review the diagnostic results to set two personal goals.

weeks.assessment: Restaurant vocabulary quiz and diagnostic conversation.

weeks.topic: The verb venir and describing a meal
objectives: Conjugate venir
Describe dishes and who comes to dinner

days.title: Venir
days.work: Learn the forms of venir (vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, venís, vienen) and complete a Conjuguemos drill to 90%.

days.title: ¿Quién viene?
days.work: Write invitations for a family dinner and sentences stating who comes, when, and from where.

days.title: Taste words
days.work: Learn delicioso, picante, salado, dulce, rico and describe five foods during a real meal.

days.title: Listening
days.work: Watch a restaurant scene video in Spanish and list what each customer orders and how they describe it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a venir and food description quiz.

objectives: Distinguish permanent traits from conditions and location
Use ser and estar correctly in context

days.title: Rules
days.work: Learn the DOCTOR (ser) and PLACE (estar) memory aids and sort 20 sentence cards.

days.title: Meaning changes
days.work: Study adjectives that change meaning (es aburrido vs. está aburrido; es rico vs. está rico) and write 6 contrasting pairs.

days.title: Food & feelings
days.work: Describe a meal: how the food is (ser) and how it tastes and is today (estar), plus how diners feel.

days.title: StudySpanish practice
days.work: Read the StudySpanish.com ser/estar lesson and complete its practice exercises.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a 25-item ser vs. estar quiz.

objectives: Order a full meal in a role-play
Read an authentic menu
materials: printed authentic menu from a Spanish or Mexican restaurant

days.title: Culture: comer fuera
days.work: Read about tapas in Spain, comida corrida in Mexico, and sobremesa, and compare meal times with yours.

days.title: Authentic menu
days.work: Read a printed authentic Spanish-language menu and answer 10 questions about dishes and prices.

days.title: Role-play prep
days.work: Write cue cards for a restaurant role-play using usted, polite requests, and venir.

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Perform the restaurant role-play with a parent from arrival to paying la cuenta.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Take the unit test: restaurant listening, menu reading, venir, and ser vs. estar.

weeks.assessment: Restaurant role-play rubric and unit 1 test.

objectives: Name rooms and furniture
Describe your bedroom

days.title: Rooms
days.work: Learn 10 rooms and draw and label a floor plan of your home.

days.title: Furniture
days.work: Learn 15 furniture items and label your bedroom with sticky notes.

days.title: Colors
days.work: Learn color words with agreement (rojo/roja, azul, marrón) and describe the colors of 10 items in your room.

days.title: Mi dormitorio
days.work: Write a 10-sentence description of your bedroom using hay, estar + prepositions, and colors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a house vocabulary quiz.

objectives: Compare people and things
Use superlatives and irregular comparatives
materials: photos of rooms or real-estate ads

days.title: Comparatives
days.work: Learn más/menos...que and tan...como and compare 10 pairs of objects in your house.

days.title: Irregulars
days.work: Learn mejor, peor, mayor, menor and compare family members' ages and skills.

days.title: Superlatives
days.work: Learn el/la más... de and write superlatives about your family, house, and town.

days.title: Real-estate ads
days.work: Read three Spanish apartment ads and compare them in eight sentences, choosing the best for your family.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a comparisons quiz.

objectives: Conjugate poder, dormir, costar, and jugar
Explain the boot pattern

days.title: The boot
days.work: Learn the stem-change 'boot' pattern and conjugate poder and dormir, noting nosotros/vosotros don't change.

days.title: More verbs
days.work: Add costar, volver, encontrar, almorzar, and jugar (u→ue) and complete a Conjuguemos stem-changer drill.

days.title: Sleep survey
days.work: Ask family ¿Cuántas horas duermes? and ¿A qué hora vuelves a casa? and graph the results.

days.title: Puedo...
days.work: Write 10 sentences about what you can and cannot do in your house using poder + infinitive.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an o→ue stem-changer quiz.

weeks.topic: Los quehaceres and affirmative tú commands
objectives: Name household chores
Give informal commands

days.title: Chores
days.work: Learn 14 chores and make a family chore chart in Spanish.

days.title: Regular tú commands
days.work: Learn that the affirmative tú command equals the él form (limpia, lava, come) and write commands for each chore.

days.title: Irregular commands
days.work: Learn di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven and complete a 20-item command practice.

days.title: Simón dice
days.work: Play Simón dice with a family member using 20 commands, then actually do three chores as commanded.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a chores and commands quiz.

objectives: Describe actions in progress
Present a home tour

days.title: Present progressive
days.work: Learn estar + -ando/-iendo, including leyendo and durmiendo, and describe what each family member is doing right now.

days.title: Picture description
days.work: Describe a busy house illustration in 10 progressive sentences.

days.title: Culture: casas
days.work: Read about homes in Spain and Latin America (interior patios, rooftop azoteas, apartment living) and write five comparisons.

days.title: Home tour
days.work: Record a 2-minute Spanish video tour of your home with comparisons and chores done in each room.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Take the unit test on house vocabulary, comparisons, stem-changers, commands, and the progressive.

weeks.assessment: Home tour video rubric and unit 2 test.

objectives: Name clothing items
Describe what people wear for different weather

days.title: Clothing
days.work: Learn 20 clothing words and label clothes from your closet.

days.title: Llevar
days.work: Describe what five family members are wearing today with llevar and colors.

days.title: Weather & clothes
days.work: Connect weather and seasons to clothing: Cuando hace frío, llevo un abrigo; write 8 sentences.

days.title: Fashion blog
days.work: Read a short teen fashion blog post in Spanish and list the items and opinions mentioned.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a clothing vocabulary quiz with a listening description.

weeks.topic: Stem-changing e→ie verbs: pensar, querer, preferir
objectives: Conjugate e→ie verbs
Express preferences and intentions about clothes

days.title: e→ie
days.work: Learn pensar, querer, preferir, empezar, entender, cerrar in the boot pattern and complete a Conjuguemos drill.

days.title: Preferences
days.work: Write 10 sentences comparing clothing choices: Prefiero la camisa roja, pero mi hermano quiere la azul.

days.title: Pensar + inf
days.work: Use pensar + infinitive to describe three upcoming plans and compare with ir a + infinitive.

days.title: Conversation
days.work: Discuss with a parent what clothes you want, prefer, and plan to buy for the next season.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an e→ie quiz with mixed o→ue items.

objectives: Point out items with este/ese/aquel
Use large numbers for prices

days.title: Demonstratives
days.work: Learn este, ese, aquel and their forms and point out clothing at three distances in 12 sentences.

days.title: Big numbers
days.work: Learn 100–1,000,000 including doscientos/quinientos/setecientos and read 20 prices aloud.

days.title: Currencies
days.work: Learn the currencies of eight Spanish-speaking countries and convert three clothing prices to dollars.

days.title: ¿Cuánto cuesta?
days.work: Practice ¿Cuánto cuesta(n)? and answer with prices and demonstratives using price-tagged items at home.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a demonstratives and numbers dictation quiz.

weeks.topic: De compras: shopping role-plays and culture
objectives: Shop for clothing in a store or market
Bargain politely in a market

days.title: Store phrases
days.work: Learn ¿En qué puedo servirle?, ¿Qué talla usa?, Me queda grande/bien, and practice a fitting-room dialogue.

days.title: Markets
days.work: Read about markets such as Chichicastenango (Guatemala) and El Rastro (Madrid) and when bargaining is appropriate.

days.title: Textiles
days.work: Watch a short video on Guatemalan Maya weaving (huipiles) and write five sentences about the product and its meaning.

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Role-play buying an outfit in a store and then bargaining for a souvenir in a market with play money.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a shopping-dialogue listening quiz.

weeks.assessment: Shopping role-play rubric and listening quiz.

objectives: Create a clothing catalog page
Integrate clothing, prices, and preferences

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a catalog page with eight items, colors, sizes, and prices in euros or pesos.

days.title: Write
days.work: Write a description for each item using demonstratives, comparisons, and e→ie verbs.

days.title: Reading
days.work: Read an authentic online store page in Spanish and answer comprehension questions.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present your catalog as a 90-second TV shopping segment.

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Take the unit 3 test on clothing, stem-changers, demonstratives, numbers, and shopping.

weeks.assessment: Catalog project rubric and unit 3 test.

objectives: Narrate completed past actions with -ar verbs
Use past time expressions

days.title: Preterite -ar
days.work: Learn the preterite -ar endings (-é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron) and conjugate comprar, hablar, and mirar.

days.title: Time expressions
days.work: Learn ayer, anoche, la semana pasada, hace dos días and write 10 sentences about last weekend.

days.title: Present vs. preterite
days.work: Contrast nosotros forms (hablamos) and identify present or past from context in 15 sentences.

days.title: Receipts
days.work: Look at three store receipts and write what each person bought and how much they paid.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a preterite -ar quiz.

objectives: Apply yo-form spelling changes
Narrate a shopping trip

days.title: Spelling rules
days.work: Learn why buscar→busqué, pagar→pagué, empezar→empecé and practice 15 yo forms.

days.title: StudySpanish practice
days.work: Complete the StudySpanish.com preterite regular-verb exercises and correct errors.

days.title: Diary
days.work: Write a 10-sentence diary entry about a shopping trip using at least five spelling-change verbs.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Ask a family member ten questions about what they did yesterday and record their answers in the preterite.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a spelling-change preterite quiz.

weeks.topic: Direct object pronouns lo, la, los, las
objectives: Replace direct objects with pronouns
Place pronouns correctly

days.title: DOPs
days.work: Learn lo/la/los/las and replace the object in 15 sentences: Compré la camisa → La compré.

days.title: Placement
days.work: Practice pronoun placement before conjugated verbs and attached to infinitives and progressives.

days.title: ¿Lo compraste?
days.work: Answer a parent's questions about purchases using pronouns: ¿Compraste los zapatos? Sí, los compré.

days.title: Gift story
days.work: Write a short story about buying gifts for three relatives using preterite and direct object pronouns.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a direct object pronoun quiz.

objectives: Review units 1–4
Demonstrate Novice Mid–High proficiency

days.title: Review: units 1–2
days.work: Review restaurant phrases, venir, ser/estar, house, comparisons, stem-changers, commands, and the progressive with a practice test.

days.title: Review: units 3–4
days.work: Review clothing, e→ie verbs, demonstratives, numbers, preterite -ar, and direct object pronouns with Conjuguemos drills.

days.title: Speaking exam
days.work: Do a 4-minute interview with a parent about your home, routine chores, clothes, and a recent shopping trip.

days.title: Written exam
days.work: Take the semester exam with listening, reading, grammar, and a 12-sentence writing prompt.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Complete a can-do checklist and set two goals for semester 2.

objectives: Name vacation places and activities
Talk about past trips

days.title: Vacation words
days.work: Learn 20 vacation places and activities and caption your own travel photos.

days.title: Preterite -ar review
days.work: Write 10 sentences about a past trip using -ar preterite verbs (visité, nadé, tomé).

days.title: Travel brochure
days.work: Read a Spanish tourism brochure for Puerto Rico and list five attractions with descriptions.

days.title: Dream trip
days.work: Choose a Spanish-speaking destination and list ten activities you could do there.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a vacation vocabulary quiz.

objectives: Conjugate -er/-ir verbs in the preterite
Narrate with mixed regular verbs

days.title: Endings
days.work: Learn the shared -er/-ir preterite endings (-í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron) and conjugate comer and salir.

days.title: Drill
days.work: Complete a Conjuguemos preterite -er/-ir drill to 90%.

days.title: Leer and oír
days.work: Learn the y-forms (leyó, leyeron, oyó) and write five sentences with them.

days.title: Trip interview
days.work: Interview a parent about their best vacation using -ar, -er, and -ir preterite questions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a mixed regular preterite quiz.

objectives: Use fui, fuiste, fue in context
Describe where you went and how it was

days.title: Ir/ser preterite
days.work: Learn that ir and ser share preterite forms and determine meaning from context in 15 sentences.

days.title: ¿Adónde fuiste?
days.work: Write where each family member went last summer and how it was: Fuimos a la playa; fue divertido.

days.title: Listening
days.work: Listen to a native speaker describe a trip (Spanish Proficiency Exercises) and note where they went and what they did.

days.title: Conversation
days.work: Have an unscripted conversation with a parent about a past trip, asking at least five follow-up questions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an ir/ser preterite quiz.

weeks.assessment: Ir/ser preterite quiz and conversation rubric.

objectives: Research a destination
Connect geography and culture

days.title: Geography
days.work: Locate eight famous sites (Machu Picchu, Chichén Itzá, Salar de Uyuni, El Yunque, la Alhambra) and identify their landforms.

days.title: Reading
days.work: Read an article in Spanish about Machu Picchu and answer comprehension questions.

days.title: Research
days.work: Research one destination's history, landforms, food, and festivals and take notes in Spanish.

days.title: Comparación
days.work: Compare your destination with a California landmark (Yosemite, Death Valley) in six sentences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share research findings orally in a 1-minute summary.

weeks.assessment: Research notes check and oral summary.

objectives: Narrate a trip in the past
Integrate all preterite forms

days.title: Sequencing
days.work: Learn primero, luego, después, más tarde, por fin and outline a trip story.

days.title: Draft
days.work: Write a 15-sentence travel blog about a real or imagined trip to your researched destination using the preterite.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Self-edit with a checklist (preterite endings, ir/ser, -car/-gar/-zar) and add photos.

days.title: Share
days.work: Present your blog aloud and answer three questions from a listener.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Take the unit 5 test on vacation vocabulary and the preterite.

weeks.assessment: Travel blog rubric and unit 5 test.

objectives: Name volunteer activities
Describe community needs

days.title: Vocabulary
days.work: Learn 18 community-service words and match them to photos of volunteer work.

days.title: Local needs
days.work: List community organizations in your town and describe in Spanish what each one does.

days.title: Reading
days.work: Read a short article about a youth volunteer project in Latin America and summarize it in five sentences.

days.title: Survey
days.work: Ask family members what volunteer work they have done and record answers in the preterite.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a community vocabulary quiz.

weeks.topic: Indirect object pronouns and the verb dar
objectives: Use me, te, le, nos, les
Say who gives what to whom

days.title: IOPs
days.work: Learn indirect object pronouns and identify the indirect object in 15 sentences.

days.title: Dar
days.work: Learn present dar (doy, das...) and preterite dar (di, diste, dio) and complete a drill.

days.title: Le/les clarification
days.work: Practice clarifying le/les with a + person: Le di la ropa a mi abuela.

days.title: Gifts and help
days.work: Write 10 sentences about what you gave or did for others using IOPs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an indirect object pronoun and dar quiz.

objectives: Conjugate hacer and decir in the preterite
Report what people did and said

days.title: Hacer
days.work: Learn hice, hiciste, hizo (z spelling), hicimos, hicieron and answer ¿Qué hiciste ayer? in 8 ways.

days.title: Decir
days.work: Learn dije, dijiste, dijo, dijimos, dijeron and report what five people said using IOPs: Me dijo que...

days.title: Practice
days.work: Complete StudySpanish.com irregular preterite practice for hacer and decir.

days.title: Culture: service
days.work: Read about César Chávez and Dolores Huerta's community organizing in California and write five preterite sentences about what they did.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take an irregular preterite quiz.

objectives: Plan and report on a service project
Present to an audience
materials: materials for a small service project

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan a small service activity (food drive, letters to seniors, park cleanup) and write the plan in Spanish.

days.title: Do it
days.work: Carry out the service activity with family and take photos.

days.title: Write
days.work: Write a 12-sentence report in the preterite on what you did, what people said, and what you gave.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the report with photos to a family audience and answer questions.

days.title: Unit 6 test
days.work: Take the unit 6 test on IOPs, dar, hacer, decir, and community vocabulary.

weeks.assessment: Service report rubric and unit 6 test.

objectives: Name film and TV genres
Give opinions about shows and movies

days.title: Genres
days.work: Learn 12 genre words and classify 15 well-known movies and shows.

days.title: Opinions
days.work: Give opinions with me parece, creo que, and adjectives like emocionante, violento, tonto.

days.title: TV listings
days.work: Read a Spanish-language TV guide and answer questions about times, channels, and genres.

days.title: Telenovelas
days.work: Read about the telenovela tradition in Mexico and Colombia and compare it with U.S. TV dramas.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a genre vocabulary and opinions quiz.

weeks.topic: Acabar de + infinitive and verbs like gustar
objectives: Say what just happened
Use aburrir, interesar, encantar, importar, quedar, faltar

days.title: Acabar de
days.work: Learn acabar de + infinitive and write 8 sentences about things you just did.

days.title: Gustar-like verbs
days.work: Learn me aburre(n), me interesa(n), me encanta(n), me importa(n), me falta(n) and write opinions about movies.

days.title: Señor Wooly
days.work: Watch a free Señor Wooly video and describe what the characters like, bore, or interest them.

days.title: Conversation
days.work: Discuss favorite movies and shows with a parent using five gustar-like verbs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a gustar-like verbs quiz.

objectives: Write and present a film review
Summarize a plot in the preterite
materials: a family film with Spanish audio or subtitles

days.title: Watch
days.work: Watch a family film with Spanish audio (e.g., Coco) with Spanish subtitles and take notes on characters.

days.title: Plot summary
days.work: Write a 10-sentence plot summary in the preterite.

days.title: Review
days.work: Add opinions with gustar-like verbs and a star rating to complete a film review.

days.title: Present
days.work: Record your film review as a 2-minute video.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Take the unit 7 test on media vocabulary, acabar de, and gustar-like verbs.

weeks.assessment: Film review rubric and unit 7 test.

objectives: Name technology and online activities
Use pedir and servir (e→i)

days.title: Tech vocabulary
days.work: Learn 18 technology words and label the parts of a computer and phone.

days.title: Pedir & servir
days.work: Learn the e→i boot pattern (pido, sirve) and complete a Conjuguemos drill, including preterite pidió/sirvió.

days.title: ¿Para qué sirve?
days.work: Explain what 8 devices or apps are for: La computadora sirve para escribir.

days.title: Survey
days.work: Survey family about daily screen use and write a report with numbers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a technology vocabulary and e→i verb quiz.

objectives: Distinguish saber and conocer
Talk about skills and people/places you know

days.title: Rules
days.work: Learn saber (facts, how to) vs. conocer (people, places) and the personal a, then sort 20 sentences.

days.title: Sé + infinitive
days.work: Write 10 sentences about tech skills you know how to do: Sé crear una página web.

days.title: Conozco
days.work: Write about people and places you know, including the personal a.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Interview a parent about their tech skills and places they know, using both verbs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a saber vs. conocer quiz.

objectives: Compare technology use across cultures
Argue a simple opinion

days.title: Infographic
days.work: Read a Spanish infographic on teen internet use in Spain or Mexico and answer questions about the data.

days.title: Comparison
days.work: Compare those statistics with U.S. teen data in six Spanish sentences.

days.title: Opinion
days.work: Write a 10-sentence opinion piece on ventajas y desventajas of phones for teens.

days.title: Debate
days.work: Hold a short debate with a parent using en mi opinión and estoy/no estoy de acuerdo.

days.title: Unit 8 test
days.work: Take the unit 8 test on technology vocabulary, pedir/servir, and saber/conocer.

weeks.assessment: Opinion piece rubric and unit 8 test.

weeks.topic: Spanish I review: present tense system
objectives: Review all Spanish I present-tense structures

days.title: Regular present
days.work: Review regular -ar/-er/-ir verbs from 1A with a timed Conjuguemos drill.

days.title: Irregular & stem-changers
days.work: Review ser, estar, ir, tener, venir and o→ue, e→ie, e→i stem-changers.

days.title: Commands & progressive
days.work: Review tú commands and the present progressive with a picture-description task.

days.title: Pronouns
days.work: Review direct and indirect object pronouns in a 20-item practice.

days.title: Practice test
days.work: Take a self-scored present-tense practice test and list your weakest areas.

weeks.topic: Spanish I review: past tense and culture
objectives: Review the preterite and cultural topics

days.title: Regular preterite
days.work: Review regular and spelling-change preterite verbs with a narrative writing task.

days.title: Irregular preterite
days.work: Review ir/ser, hacer, decir, and dar in the preterite with a story-retelling activity.

days.title: Culture review
days.work: Review the year's culture topics (tapas, homes, markets, destinations, telenovelas) with a self-made quiz.

days.title: Reading practice
days.work: Read two authentic texts (a blog post and an ad) and answer questions.

days.title: Speaking practice
days.work: Practice a mock 5-minute conversation covering all year's topics.

weeks.topic: Spanish I final integrated performance assessment
objectives: Demonstrate Novice High proficiency in all three modes

days.title: Interpretive
days.work: Read an authentic text and listen to a native-speaker clip, answering comprehension and inference questions.

days.title: Interpersonal
days.work: Hold a 5-minute unscripted conversation about home, shopping, a past trip, and technology.

days.title: Presentational writing
days.work: Write a 15–20 sentence narrative about a memorable day using present and preterite.

days.title: Presentational speaking

courses.subject: VAPA
courses.title: Visual and Performing Arts 8
courses.description: A year-long arts survey aligned to the 2019 California Arts Standards for grade 8. Students rotate through visual arts (perspective drawing, portraiture, painting), music (notation, keyboard, composing, American music history), theatre (acting, scene study, playwriting), media arts (photography and stop-motion animation) and dance (choreography), building a portfolio and ending with a home exhibition and performance.
courses.framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools, Prekindergarten Through Grade Twelve; 2020 California Arts Education Framework

standards.VA:Cr1.1.8: Document early stages of the creative process visually and/or verbally in traditional or new media.
standards.VA:Cr1.2.8: Collaboratively shape an artistic investigation of an aspect of present-day life using a contemporary practice of art and design.
standards.VA:Cr2.1.8: Demonstrate willingness to experiment, innovate and take risks to pursue ideas, forms and meanings that emerge in the process of art-making.
standards.VA:Cr2.2.8: Demonstrate awareness of ethical responsibility to oneself and others when posting and sharing content online.
standards.VA:Cr3.1.8: Apply relevant criteria to examine, reflect on and plan revisions for a work of art in progress.
standards.VA:Pr5.1.8: Collaboratively prepare and present selected theme-based artwork for display, and formulate exhibition narratives for the viewer.
standards.VA:Pr6.1.8: Analyze why and how an exhibition or collection may influence ideas, beliefs and experiences.
standards.VA:Re7.1.8: Explain how a person's aesthetic choices are influenced by culture and environment and impact the visual image one conveys to others.
standards.VA:Re7.2.8: Compare and contrast contexts and media in which viewers encounter images that influence ideas, emotions and actions.
standards.VA:Re8.1.8: Interpret art by analyzing how the interaction of subject matter, characteristics of form and structure, use of media, art-making approaches and relevant contextual information contributes to understanding.
standards.VA:Re9.1.8: Create a convincing and logical argument to support an evaluation of art.
standards.VA:Cn11.1.8: Distinguish different ways art is used to represent, establish, reinforce and reflect group identity.
standards.MU:Cr1.1.8: Generate rhythmic, melodic and harmonic phrases and harmonic accompaniments within expanded forms that convey expressive intent.
standards.MU:Cr2.1.8: Select, organize and document personal musical ideas for arrangements, songs and compositions within expanded forms.
standards.MU:Cr3.2.8: Present the final version of a documented personal composition, song or arrangement demonstrating unity, variety and development.
standards.MU:Pr4.2.8: Compare the structure of contrasting pieces of music selected for performance, explaining how the elements of music are used in each.
standards.MU:Pr5.1.8: Identify and apply personally developed criteria to rehearse, refine and determine when the music is ready to perform.
standards.MU:Pr6.1.8: Perform music with technical accuracy, stylistic expression and culturally authentic practices to convey the creator's intent.
standards.MU:Re7.2.8: Compare how the elements of music and expressive qualities relate to the structure within programs of music.
standards.MU:Re8.1.8: Support personal interpretation of contrasting programs of music and explain how creators or performers apply the elements of music to convey intent.
standards.MU:Cn11.0.8: Demonstrate understanding of relationships between music and the other arts, other disciplines, varied contexts and daily life.
standards.TH:Cr1.1.8: Imagine and explore multiple perspectives and solutions to staging problems in a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cr2.1.8: Articulate and apply critical analysis, background knowledge, research and historical and cultural context to the development of original ideas for a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Cr3.1.8: Use repetition and analysis to revise devised or scripted drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Pr4.1.8: Develop a physical and vocal characterization appropriate to a character's objectives in a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Pr5.1.8: Use a variety of acting techniques to increase skills in a rehearsal or drama/theatre performance.
standards.TH:Pr6.1.8: Perform a rehearsed drama/theatre work for an audience.
standards.TH:Re8.1.8: Recognize and share artistic choices when participating in or observing a drama/theatre work.
standards.TH:Re9.1.8: Respond to a drama/theatre work using supporting evidence, personal aesthetics and artistic criteria.
standards.TH:Cn11.2.8: Research the story elements of a staged drama/theatre work and discuss how a playwright might have intended it to be produced.
standards.MA:Cr1.1.8: Generate ideas, goals and solutions for original media artworks through application of focused creative processes.
standards.MA:Cr2.1.8: Design, propose and evaluate artistic ideas, plans, prototypes and production processes for media arts productions.
standards.MA:Cr3.1.8: Implement production processes to integrate content and stylistic conventions for determined meaning in media arts productions.
standards.MA:Pr6.1.8: Design the presentation and distribution of media artworks through multiple formats.
standards.MA:Re7.1.8: Analyze the intent, meanings and influence of a variety of media artworks.
standards.DA:Cr1.1.8: Implement the elements of dance to develop choreographic content using a variety of stimuli.
standards.DA:Cr2.1.8: Collaborate to select and apply a variety of choreographic devices and dance structures to choreograph an original dance study.
standards.DA:Pr4.1.8: Use body-designs and spatial relationships with intent and clarity, adapting to performance space.
standards.DA:Pr6.1.8: Perform dance using artistic expression and a variety of production elements for a live or recorded audience.
standards.DA:Re8.1.8: Select a dance and explain how the artistic expression is achieved through relationships among the elements of dance, use of body, technique and context.

objectives: Use contour and blind contour drawing to improve observation
Start a sketchbook documenting the creative process

days.title: Sketchbook setup
days.work: Decorate a sketchbook cover and do 5 one-minute gesture drawings of a family member or pet.

days.title: Blind contour
days.work: Do three blind contour drawings of your hand without looking at the paper; write what you noticed.

days.title: Contour drawing
days.work: Draw a shoe in modified contour line, looking 80% at the object.

days.title: Cross-contour
days.work: Add cross-contour lines to a drawing of a banana or mug to show form.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Choose your best drawing and write a reflection on progress.

objectives: Create a 9-step value scale
Render 3-D forms using light and shadow

days.title: Value scale
days.work: Make a 9-step value scale and a smooth gradient bar.

days.title: Shading techniques
days.work: Practice hatching, cross-hatching, stippling and blending in 4 squares.

days.title: Shading spheres
days.work: Shade a sphere lit by a lamp showing highlight, core shadow and cast shadow.

days.title: Still life
days.work: Draw a lit still life of an egg, mug and box with a full value range.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Self-critique using a value checklist and revise the darkest darks.

weeks.assessment: Still-life drawing graded with a value rubric.

objectives: Use horizon line, vanishing point and orthogonals
Draw a room or hallway in one-point perspective

days.title: Perspective basics
days.work: Draw boxes above, on and below the horizon line using one vanishing point.

days.title: Block letters
days.work: Draw your initials in one-point perspective block letters.

days.title: Hallway or road
days.work: Draw a hallway, road or railroad track receding to a vanishing point.

days.title: Room interior
days.work: Draw your bedroom in one-point perspective with furniture.

days.title: Review
days.work: Add value to the room drawing and check lines with a ruler.

objectives: Draw forms in two-point perspective
Analyze perspective in Renaissance and modern art

days.title: Two-point boxes
days.work: Draw 6 boxes in two-point perspective above, at and below eye level.

days.title: Building a house
days.work: Draw a house with roof, doors and windows in two-point perspective.

days.title: Art history
days.work: Analyze perspective in Raphael's 'School of Athens' and a modern cityscape on Google Arts & Culture.

days.title: Cityscape
days.work: Begin an original cityscape with at least 5 buildings.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Ink and shade the cityscape.

objectives: Complete a finished drawing using line, value and perspective
Critique artwork with criteria

days.title: Plan
days.work: Thumbnail 3 compositions for 'A place that matters to me.'

days.title: Draft
days.work: Lightly sketch the chosen composition.

days.title: Render
days.work: Add value and detail.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Complete the drawing and sign it.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Write a critique using describe, analyze, interpret, evaluate.

objectives: Draw a face using classical proportion guidelines
Observe how real faces vary from the 'ideal'

days.title: Proportion guide
days.work: Draw an oval head with guidelines: eyes halfway down, nose at one-third, mouth at one-third of the remaining distance; label each.

days.title: Eyes and noses
days.work: Fill a sketchbook page with 4 eyes and 4 noses drawn from a mirror, shading the eyelid and nostril shadows.

days.title: Mouths and ears
days.work: Draw 4 mouths (neutral, smiling, open, profile) and 2 ears, noting where ears line up with eyes and nose.

days.title: Measuring real faces
days.work: Photograph or observe three family members and record how their proportions differ from the guideline face.

days.title: Self-portrait sketch
days.work: Draw a full self-portrait from a mirror using the guidelines, then compare it to a photo and note one correction.

objectives: Mix a 12-part color wheel and value scales
Use color schemes intentionally to express mood
materials: acrylic or tempera paints in red, yellow, blue, white, black

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Mix and paint a 12-part color wheel of primary, secondary and tertiary colors.

days.title: Tints, shades, tones
days.work: Paint a 7-step tint-to-shade strip for one hue and a tone strip adding gray.

days.title: Color schemes
days.work: Paint the same simple landscape thumbnail 4 times in complementary, analogous, monochromatic and warm/cool schemes.

days.title: Color and mood in art
days.work: Compare Picasso's 'The Old Guitarist' (Blue Period) and Matisse's 'The Dessert: Harmony in Red' and explain how color shapes mood.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on color vocabulary and write which of your 4 thumbnails best conveys a chosen mood and why.

weeks.assessment: Color wheel, scheme studies and quiz.

objectives: Analyze how portraits use symbols, pose and setting to express identity
Plan a symbolic identity portrait
materials: Smithsonian National Portrait Gallery images (via Learning Lab or Google Arts & Culture)

days.title: Presidential portraits
days.work: Compare Gilbert Stuart's 'Lansdowne' portrait of Washington with Kehinde Wiley's portrait of Barack Obama; list how each uses pose and background.

days.title: Frida Kahlo
days.work: Analyze Frida Kahlo's 'Self-Portrait with Thorn Necklace and Hummingbird' and explain the meaning of three symbols.

days.title: Group identity
days.work: Examine portraits from a culture or community you belong to and write how art reinforces group identity.

days.title: Plan your portrait
days.work: List 5 symbols, colors and a setting that represent you and sketch 3 thumbnail compositions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Choose one plan, get feedback from a family member, and revise the composition sketch on final paper.

weeks.assessment: Identity portrait plan with symbol key.

objectives: Paint a portrait using an intentional color scheme
Evaluate and defend artistic choices in an artist statement

days.title: Underpainting
days.work: Transfer the sketch and block in large areas with thin underpainting in your chosen scheme.

days.title: Building layers
days.work: Add mid-tones and shadows to the face and background, mixing skin tones from primaries.

days.title: Symbols and details
days.work: Paint symbolic objects and fine details with small brushes; add highlights last.

days.title: Finishing
days.work: Refine edges, check values by squinting, and sign the finished portrait.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Write a 150-word artist statement explaining symbols and color choices and evaluate the portrait using a 4-criterion rubric.

objectives: Read and perform rhythms with whole through sixteenth notes and rests
Count in 4/4, 3/4 and 6/8

days.title: Note values
days.work: Complete the musictheory.net lessons on note durations and rests; clap and count 8 one-measure patterns.

days.title: Time signatures
days.work: Count and tap rhythms in 4/4, 3/4 and 6/8 with a metronome at 80 bpm.

days.title: Syncopation
days.work: Clap syncopated patterns and identify syncopation in a song like Scott Joplin's 'The Entertainer.'

days.title: Body percussion
days.work: Compose and perform a 4-measure body-percussion rhythm (stomp, clap, snap, pat).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a rhythm dictation of 4 measures and perform a sight-reading rhythm at 80 bpm.

objectives: Identify notes in treble and bass clefs
Read simple melodies

days.title: Treble clef
days.work: Learn line and space names in treble clef and reach 20 correct in a row on the musictheory.net note trainer.

days.title: Bass clef
days.work: Learn bass clef names and repeat the note-trainer goal.

days.title: Accidentals
days.work: Learn sharps, flats and naturals and find them on a keyboard diagram.

days.title: Intervals
days.work: Identify seconds through octaves by sight and by ear using 'Here Comes the Bride' (4th) and 'Twinkle' (5th) references.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Note-naming and interval quiz.

objectives: Play a C major scale with correct fingering
Build major scales using whole and half steps
materials: keyboard, piano or free online keyboard app

days.title: Keyboard geography
days.work: Locate all Cs and play C-D-E-F-G five-finger patterns in each hand.

days.title: C major scale
days.work: Practice the C major scale hands separately with thumb-under fingering at 60 bpm.

days.title: Building scales
days.work: Use the W-W-H-W-W-W-H formula to build G and F major scales and play them.

days.title: Simple melody
days.work: Learn 'Ode to Joy' right hand from notation.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play the C major scale and 'Ode to Joy' for a family member and self-evaluate with a checklist.

objectives: Build major and minor triads
Accompany a melody with I-IV-V chords

days.title: Triads
days.work: Build C, F and G major triads and compare major and minor triads on Chrome Music Lab.

days.title: I-IV-V
days.work: Play the I-IV-V-I progression in C with the left hand.

days.title: Twelve-bar blues
days.work: Play the 12-bar blues progression in C.

days.title: Accompanying
days.work: Accompany 'Ode to Joy' with left-hand chords.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the 12-bar blues progression with a steady beat.

objectives: Prepare and perform a short piece
Compare structure in contrasting pieces
materials: recordings of Beethoven 'Für Elise' and a pop song

days.title: Form listening
days.work: Listen to 'Für Elise' and diagram its rondo form (A-B-A-C-A).

days.title: Contrasting structures
days.work: Compare the verse-chorus form of a pop song with 'Für Elise' using a chart of form, dynamics and tempo.

days.title: Rehearsal
days.work: Rehearse your chosen piece with dynamics and articulation markings, setting personal criteria for 'ready.'

days.title: Recording
days.work: Record a performance and listen back for accuracy.

days.title: Recital
days.work: Perform for family and complete a self-evaluation.

weeks.topic: Spirituals, work songs and the blues
objectives: Trace the roots of American music in African American traditions
Identify blues form and call and response
materials: recordings via Library of Congress or Smithsonian Folkways

days.title: Spirituals
days.work: Listen to the Fisk Jubilee Singers and analyze 'Swing Low, Sweet Chariot' (connects to HSS slavery unit).

days.title: Work songs
days.work: Listen to work songs and identify call-and-response patterns.

days.title: The blues
days.work: Listen to Bessie Smith and B.B. King; identify 12-bar form and AAB lyric pattern.

days.title: Writing blues lyrics
days.work: Write a 3-verse blues lyric in AAB form about a frustration in your life.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform your blues lyrics over the 12-bar progression.

objectives: Identify ragtime, swing and improvisation
Explain how jazz musicians apply the elements of music
materials: recordings (Scott Joplin, Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Ella Fitzgerald)

days.title: Ragtime
days.work: Listen to Scott Joplin's 'Maple Leaf Rag' and identify syncopation.

days.title: Louis Armstrong
days.work: Listen to 'West End Blues' and analyze the trumpet improvisation.

days.title: Big band
days.work: Compare Duke Ellington's 'Take the A Train' with a modern big band.

days.title: Improvisation
days.work: Improvise on the C blues scale over a backing track.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Listening quiz identifying genres and instruments.

objectives: Generate melodic phrases with expressive intent
Organize phrases into a form

days.title: Motifs
days.work: Create 4 two-measure motifs in Song Maker and choose the strongest.

days.title: Phrases
days.work: Develop the motif into an 8-measure phrase with a question-answer structure.

days.title: Form
days.work: Organize phrases into ABA form.

days.title: Harmony
days.work: Add chords under your melody.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share a draft with family and record feedback.

objectives: Revise and present a documented composition
Explain choices
materials: Song Maker or notation app (MuseScore free)

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise for unity and variety based on feedback.

days.title: Notate
days.work: Notate the final version in MuseScore or by hand.

days.title: Program notes
days.work: Write program notes explaining your expressive intent.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse or finalize the digital performance.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the composition and program notes.

objectives: Use vocal and physical warm-ups
Explore how voice and body create character

days.title: Vocal warm-ups
days.work: Practice breathing, projection and 5 tongue twisters ('red leather, yellow leather'); record before and after.

days.title: Physical warm-ups
days.work: Do a mirror exercise and a walk exploring how different characters lead with head, chest or hips.

days.title: Tableau
days.work: Create 3 frozen tableaux showing a scene from a fairy tale and photograph them.

days.title: Character walk
days.work: Develop a character's walk, posture and voice from a one-sentence description.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a 30-second character introduction using voice and body.

objectives: Identify a character's objective, obstacle and tactics
Apply them in improvisation

days.title: Objectives
days.work: Learn objective-obstacle-tactic and analyze a scene from a familiar film.

days.title: Improvisation
days.work: Improvise 3 two-person scenes where each character wants something different.

days.title: Subtext
days.work: Say the line 'I'm fine' 5 ways with different subtext.

days.title: Script analysis
days.work: Break a short scene into beats and mark objectives.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform an improvised scene and identify your tactics.

objectives: Select, analyze and memorize a monologue
Research the play's context
materials: monologue from a public-domain play (e.g., Puck's epilogue, a scene from 'Our Town'-style texts in the library)

days.title: Selecting
days.work: Read 4 age-appropriate monologues and choose one.

days.title: Research
days.work: Research the play's story, playwright and period.

days.title: Analysis
days.work: Mark objectives, beats and emphasis.

days.title: Memorize
days.work: Memorize using the line-by-line method.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform off-book for family.

objectives: Rehearse a two-person scene with blocking
Use feedback to improve

days.title: Read-through
days.work: Read a two-person scene and discuss characters.

days.title: Blocking
days.work: Block the scene using stage directions.

days.title: Rehearsal
days.work: Rehearse focusing on listening and reacting.

days.title: Polish
days.work: Polish with props and costume pieces.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the scene and record it.

objectives: Analyze artistic choices in a recorded production
Write a theatre review
materials: recorded production (PBS Great Performances or a free filmed school production)

days.title: Watch part 1
days.work: Watch the first half of a recorded production and note design choices.

days.title: Watch part 2
days.work: Finish the production and note acting choices.

days.title: Analyzing choices
days.work: Analyze how set, costume and lighting support the story.

days.title: Review writing
days.work: Write a 300-word theatre review with evidence.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share the review and discuss.

objectives: Generate ideas for an original short play
Structure a plot with conflict and resolution

days.title: Story sources
days.work: Brainstorm 10 premises from news stories, history (e.g., a Gold Rush camp) and personal experience.

days.title: Choosing a premise
days.work: Choose one and write a one-paragraph premise naming characters, setting and central conflict.

days.title: Plot structure
days.work: Outline exposition, rising action, climax and resolution for a 5–8 minute play.

days.title: Character sketches
days.work: Write character sketches with objectives and obstacles for 2–3 characters.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Pitch the play to family and revise based on questions.

objectives: Write dialogue and stage directions in proper script format
Solve staging problems

days.title: Script format
days.work: Study script format and write the opening page.

days.title: Draft scene 1
days.work: Draft the first half with dialogue revealing character.

days.title: Draft scene 2
days.work: Draft the climax and resolution.

days.title: Staging problems
days.work: Identify two staging challenges (e.g., a storm, a crowd) and write creative solutions in stage directions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete the first draft and read it aloud alone, marking lines that sound unnatural.

objectives: Revise a script using a table read
Give and receive specific feedback

days.title: Table read
days.work: Hold a table read with family members reading parts.

days.title: Feedback
days.work: Collect feedback with a glow-and-grow form.

days.title: Revising dialogue
days.work: Revise dialogue for clarity and character voice.

days.title: Revising structure
days.work: Cut or add scenes to improve pacing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Finalize the second draft.

objectives: Rehearse and perform a staged reading of the original play
Reflect on the process

days.title: Casting & planning
days.work: Cast family or friends and plan simple props and set.

days.title: Rehearsal 1
days.work: Rehearse with blocking.

days.title: Rehearsal 2
days.work: Run-through with props and sound effects.

days.title: Performance
days.work: Perform the staged reading for an audience and record it.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a reflection on what worked and what you would change.

Analyze intent in famous photographs

days.work: Analyze Dorothea Lange's 'Migrant Mother' and Ansel Adams's Yosemite images for composition and intent.

days.title: Rule of thirds
days.work: Take 10 photos using a rule-of-thirds grid.

days.title: Leading lines & framing
days.work: Take 10 photos using leading lines and natural frames around the house or neighborhood.

days.work: Photograph one object from 5 viewpoints (bird's eye, worm's eye) and compare.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Select your 5 best photos and caption each with the technique used.

weeks.assessment: Photo portfolio of 5 images with captions.

objectives: Create a photo essay telling a story
Analyze how images in media influence viewers
Practice ethical sharing

days.title: Media influence
days.work: Compare how the same event is shown in news photos, ads and social media and how each influences viewers.

days.title: Planning a photo essay
days.work: Plan a 10-photo essay on 'A day in my community.'

days.title: Shooting
days.work: Shoot photos following the plan.

days.title: Editing
days.work: Edit photos (crop, exposure) and sequence them.

days.title: Ethical sharing
days.work: Write captions, get consent from people pictured, and present the photo essay.

Understand frame rate

days.work: Make a 3-second test animation of a bouncing ball.

days.work: Build characters and set.

Analyze audience response

days.title: Shooting 2
days.work: Shoot the second half.

days.title: Editing & sound
days.work: Edit the frames and add music or sound effects.

days.title: Titles & credits
days.work: Add titles and credits.

days.title: Premiere
days.work: Screen the animation for family and collect feedback.

Analyze dance works

days.work: Learn the elements of dance through movement exploration.

days.title: Dance styles
days.work: Watch Alvin Ailey's 'Revelations' excerpt and a folk dance; compare.

days.title: Improvising
days.work: Improvise movement to 3 contrasting pieces of music.

days.work: Perform and describe the phrase.

Structure an original dance study

days.work: Learn repetition, canon, unison and retrograde by applying each to your phrase.

days.title: Structure
days.work: Organize phrases into ABA form.

days.title: Spatial design
days.work: Use levels and pathways intentionally.

days.title: Collaboration
days.work: Teach part of your dance to a family member and create a duet.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Record the draft dance.

objectives: Perform an original dance with expression
Reflect on artistic choices

days.title: Rehearsal
days.work: Rehearse focusing on expression.

days.title: Production elements
days.work: Add costume and lighting.

days.title: Dress rehearsal
days.work: Run-through.

days.title: Performance
days.work: Perform and record.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write about choices.

objectives: Select and prepare work for exhibition
Write exhibition narratives

days.title: Selection
days.work: Review the year's work and select 8–10 pieces.

days.title: Mounting
days.work: Mount or mat 2-D works.

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: Physical Education 8
courses.description: Eighth-grade physical education that builds on grade 7 by emphasizing team strategy, leadership and the science of exercise. Students compare fitness results to last year, measure skill-related fitness, play new invasion, net, target and striking/fielding games (flag football, team handball, tennis, table tennis, golf, cricket), learn safe resistance training and how body systems adapt, explore social dance and mind-body fitness, compete in multi-part track events, and finish by designing, following and evaluating a two-week personal fitness plan. Sessions work in a yard, park or community center with family or a homeschool group.
courses.framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards (Grade 8); 2009 CA Physical Education Framework

standards.PE-8.1.1: Demonstrate mature, efficient form in team physical activities by combining and applying movement skills in complex game situations.
standards.PE-8.1.2: Demonstrate offensive, defensive and transition skills (cutting, screening, zone and person-to-person defense) in team invasion games.
standards.PE-8.1.3: Demonstrate advanced striking, serving and volleying skills with implements in net/wall and target games.
standards.PE-8.1.4: Perform social, square and contemporary dances with correct timing, partner etiquette and transitions.
standards.PE-8.1.5: Demonstrate technique in multi-part individual events (hurdles, relays, triple jump) and outdoor/lifetime activities.
standards.PE-8.2.1: Analyze and select offensive and defensive tactics (give-and-go, zone defense, set plays) appropriate to a game situation.
standards.PE-8.2.2: Analyze a movement or skill using biomechanical concepts (levers, angle of release, force absorption, momentum) and give corrective feedback.
standards.PE-8.2.3: Explain how practice schedules, feedback and mental rehearsal improve skill learning.
standards.PE-8.3.1: Participate in moderate-to-vigorous physical activity at least four days each week, including activities outside of class.
standards.PE-8.3.2: Assess health- and skill-related fitness components (agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time, speed) and interpret results.
standards.PE-8.3.3: Meet Healthy Fitness Zone standards for aerobic capacity, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility and body composition.
standards.PE-8.3.4: Develop, implement and evaluate a two-week personal fitness plan that applies the principles of training.
standards.PE-8.4.1: Explain how the muscular, skeletal, cardiorespiratory and nervous systems respond and adapt to exercise.
standards.PE-8.4.2: Identify major muscle groups and select exercises with safe technique (resistance bands, body weight, light free weights) to strengthen each.
standards.PE-8.4.3: Explain the role of nutrition, hydration and sleep in physical performance and recovery.
standards.PE-8.4.4: Describe how physical activity reduces stress and improves mental and emotional health.
standards.PE-8.5.1: Organize and lead group activities, demonstrating responsible leadership, rules knowledge and etiquette.
standards.PE-8.5.2: Accept responsibility for team success, resolve conflicts respectfully and include others of differing abilities.
standards.PE-8.5.3: Evaluate personal progress toward goals and identify the motivation and barriers that affect lifelong activity.

units.title: Fitness Check-In and Skill-Related Fitness
units.big_idea: Health-related fitness keeps you well; skill-related fitness helps you perform—both can be measured and improved.

units.title: Adventure Challenges and Team Leadership
units.big_idea: Leadership means organizing others, solving problems together and including everyone.

units.title: Invasion Games: Flag Football and Team Handball
units.big_idea: Set plays, transitions and defensive systems turn individual skills into team success.

units.title: Net and Wall Games: Tennis, Table Tennis and Advanced Volleyball
units.big_idea: Spin, placement and team rotations add tactical depth to net games.

units.title: Exercise Science and Resistance Training
units.big_idea: Body systems adapt to training; safe technique, nutrition and sleep make training effective.

units.title: Target and Striking/Fielding Games
units.big_idea: Accuracy depends on consistent mechanics and controlling force and angle.

units.title: Social, Square and Contemporary Dance
units.big_idea: Partner and group dance build rhythm, cooperation and cardiovascular fitness.

units.title: Mind-Body Fitness and Stress Management
units.big_idea: Yoga, breathing and mindful movement build flexibility and reduce stress.

units.title: Track and Field: Multi-Part Events
units.big_idea: Complex events are mastered by breaking them into phases and practicing each.

units.title: Lifetime Activities and Two-Week Fitness Plan
units.big_idea: Choosing activities you enjoy and planning around barriers keeps you active for life.

objectives: Re-test grade 7 FITNESSGRAM items
Compare results to last year and the Healthy Fitness Zone

days.title: Lead the warm-up
days.work: Lead a family member or sibling through the 10-move dynamic warm-up learned in grade 7, then run 10 minutes of tag-style games.

days.title: PACER re-test
days.work: Complete the 20-meter PACER (or timed mile) and record your score next to last year's.

days.title: Strength re-test
days.work: Complete curl-ups and 90-degree push-ups to cadence and record repetitions.

days.title: Flexibility re-test
days.work: Complete the back-saver sit-and-reach and trunk lift; record both sides.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Graph grade 7 vs. grade 8 scores for each item and write which components improved or declined and why.

weeks.assessment: Completed fitness comparison graph with written analysis.

objectives: Define the six skill-related fitness components
Measure agility, balance, power, reaction time, speed and coordination

days.title: Six components
days.work: Learn the six skill-related components and match each to a sport skill (e.g., power = volleyball spike); do a 20-minute circuit of one drill per component.

days.title: Agility and speed
days.work: Run the Illinois agility course set up with cones and a 40-yard dash; record best of two trials.

days.title: Power
days.work: Measure standing long jump and vertical jump (chalk-on-wall method); record best of three.

days.title: Balance and reaction
days.work: Time a one-leg stork stand with eyes closed and do the ruler-drop reaction test five times; convert drop distance to reaction time.

days.title: Profile
days.work: Create a skill-related fitness profile chart and identify your strongest and weakest component.

objectives: Write SMART goals for one health- and one skill-related component
Identify personal barriers and motivators

days.title: Motivation
days.work: Sort a list of reasons people exercise into intrinsic and extrinsic, then list your own top three motivators; finish with a 20-minute jog/walk interval.

days.title: Barriers
days.work: Identify three barriers to being active (time, weather, screens) and write a strategy for each; complete a 15-minute body-weight circuit.

days.title: SMART goals
days.work: Write two SMART goals (one health-related, one skill-related) with a weekly action step for each.

days.title: Activity log
days.work: Begin a 4-day-per-week MVPA log and do a 30-minute activity of your choice outside of class.

days.title: Check
days.work: Share goals with a parent, who signs the goal sheet; play an active game of choice.

weeks.assessment: Signed SMART goal sheet and first week of activity log.

objectives: Solve group physical challenges
Reflect on communication and trust

days.title: Tarp flip
days.work: With a group (siblings, co-op), stand on a tarp and flip it over without stepping off; debrief what worked.

days.title: Blind maze
days.work: Guide a blindfolded partner through a cone maze using only verbal directions, then switch roles.

days.title: Helium hoop
days.work: Lower a hula hoop to the ground as a group using only fingertips; try three strategies.

days.title: Raft crossing
days.work: Cross a 10-meter 'river' using only four carpet squares or pool noodles as a group.

days.title: Debrief
days.work: Write a reflection on which communication behaviors helped or hurt the group and one thing you will do differently.

objectives: Plan and lead a warm-up and game
Adapt activities so everyone can participate

days.title: Leadership styles
days.work: Discuss what makes a good coach or team captain; list five leadership behaviors.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Write a 20-minute plan: warm-up, one tag or relay game with rules, and cool-down.

days.title: Modify
days.work: Write two modifications so a younger sibling or someone with limited mobility can play your game fully.

days.title: Lead
days.work: Lead your planned session for family or a homeschool group, explaining rules and safety clearly.

days.title: Evaluate
days.work: Collect a quick thumbs-up/down from participants and self-evaluate your leadership on a rubric.

weeks.assessment: Leadership rubric for the led session.

weeks.topic: Flag football: throwing, catching and routes
objectives: Throw a spiral with correct grip and release
Run basic pass routes

days.title: Spiral grip
days.work: Practice the laces grip, step and follow-through; complete 50 partner throws at 10 yards.

days.title: Catching
days.work: Practice the diamond (above chest) and basket (below chest) catch positions on 40 partner throws.

days.title: Routes
days.work: Run slant, out, post and curl routes against air; partner throws on time.

days.title: Flag pulling
days.work: Practice flag-pulling defense and evasive moves (juke, spin) in a 1-v-1 grid.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Video a partner's throw and identify one biomechanical fix (step foot, elbow height, release point).

weeks.topic: Flag football: plays and game play
objectives: Design and run offensive plays
Use zone and person-to-person pass defense

days.title: Draw plays
days.work: Draw three plays (one run, two pass) on a play card with routes for each player.

days.title: Run plays
days.work: Walk through, then run the plays at full speed in 3-v-3 or 2-v-2.

days.title: Defense
days.work: Practice person-to-person and zone coverage and compare which stops short passes better.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play a 5-on-5 or small-sided flag football game with rotating quarterbacks.

days.title: Check
days.work: Self-assess play execution and sportsmanship; take a rules quiz (downs, rushing, scoring).

objectives: Perform the jump shot, bounce pass and three-step rule
Understand the goal area

days.title: Intro
days.work: Learn team handball's origins and rules (3 seconds, 3 steps, goal area); play a passing keep-away game.

days.title: Passing
days.work: Practice shoulder, bounce and wrist passes on the move in triangle passing drills.

days.title: Shooting
days.work: Practice the step shot and jump shot from outside a taped 6-meter arc at a cone goal.

days.title: Goalkeeping
days.work: Take turns as goalkeeper practicing ready stance and blocking low and high shots.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a skills check: 10 passes on the move and 5 shots on goal; record results.

weeks.topic: Team handball: transition and game play
objectives: Execute fast breaks
Use a give-and-go and defensive positioning

days.title: Give-and-go
days.work: Practice the give-and-go and the cut to open space in 2-v-1 drills.

days.title: Fast break
days.work: Practice transitioning from defense to a 3-on-2 fast break after a goalkeeper save.

days.title: Screens
days.work: Learn how to set and use a screen to free a shooter.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play a small-sided handball game, rotating positions every 5 minutes.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Write a comparison of strategies in handball, soccer and basketball (all invasion games).

objectives: Officiate a game fairly
Apply team strategy in tournament play

days.title: Officiating
days.work: Learn hand signals and common fouls for flag football and handball.

days.title: Tournament day 1
days.work: Play round-robin games; take turns officiating one game.

days.title: Tournament day 2
days.work: Play the second round; your team plans a strategy before each game.

days.title: Finals
days.work: Play championship games and run the scoreboard.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on teamwork, officiating fairness and how you handled a conflict.

objectives: Perform the forehand and two-hand backhand
Serve overhand into a target box

days.title: Grip and ready
days.work: Learn the eastern forehand grip and ready position; rally against a wall for 10 minutes.

days.title: Forehand
days.work: Practice drop-and-hit forehands, focusing on low-to-high swing for topspin.

days.title: Backhand
days.work: Practice the two-hand backhand from a partner toss.

days.title: Serve
days.work: Practice the overhand serve with the 'trophy' position into a chalked target box.

days.title: Check
days.work: Self-video a forehand and compare it to a skill checklist (turn, contact point, follow-through).

weeks.topic: Tennis and table tennis: rallies and scoring
objectives: Rally cooperatively and competitively
Keep score in tennis and table tennis

days.title: Tennis rallies
days.work: Rally cooperatively with a partner aiming for 10 consecutive hits.

days.title: Tennis scoring
days.work: Learn love-15-30-40-deuce scoring and play a tiebreaker game.

days.title: Table tennis
days.work: Learn the shakehand grip, push and forehand drive on a table or improvised surface.

days.title: Spin
days.work: Experiment with topspin and backspin in table tennis and describe how the ball reacts.

days.title: Mini-match
days.work: Play a best-of-three table tennis match to 11 and a short tennis set.

weeks.assessment: Scoring quiz and match play observation.

weeks.topic: Advanced volleyball: spike, block and rotation
objectives: Perform an approach and spike
Rotate and use a 3-hit offense

days.title: Review
days.work: Review grade 7 forearm pass and set with 50 partner contacts each.

days.title: Approach
days.work: Learn the 3-step spike approach (left-right-left) and arm swing using a tossed ball.

days.title: Block
days.work: Practice the two-hand block footwork and timing at the net.

days.title: Rotation
days.work: Learn 6-player rotation and practice pass-set-hit sequences in small groups.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play a modified game requiring three contacts before returning the ball.

objectives: Explain blocked vs. random practice
Give peer feedback using biomechanics

days.title: Practice types
days.work: Learn blocked vs. random practice; do 10 minutes of each with tennis forehands and note the difference.

days.title: Mental rehearsal
days.work: Visualize a serve for 2 minutes before 20 serves and compare accuracy to 20 serves without it.

days.title: Peer coaching
days.work: Coach a partner on one net-game skill using a 'praise-fix-praise' feedback format.

days.title: Choice tournament
days.work: Play a mini-tournament in the net game of your choice.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a written test on net-game strategy, scoring and practice principles.

objectives: Explain short-term responses to exercise
Explain long-term training adaptations

days.title: Short-term responses
days.work: Record heart rate, breathing rate and skin temperature at rest, after 5 minutes of jogging, and after 5 minutes of rest.

days.title: Cardiorespiratory
days.work: Learn how stroke volume and cardiac output increase with training; do a 25-minute interval run.

days.title: Muscles and bones
days.work: Explain how resistance exercise builds muscle and bone density; do a plyometric circuit (jumps, skips).

days.title: Nervous system
days.work: Explain how practice builds neuromuscular coordination; do a 15-minute footwork ladder drill.

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a diagram showing how four body systems respond and adapt to exercise.

weeks.topic: Major muscles and safe resistance training
objectives: Identify 10 major muscle groups
Perform exercises with safe technique

days.title: Muscle map
days.work: Label a muscle chart with 10 major muscles and one exercise for each.

days.title: Lower body
days.work: Learn proper squat, lunge and glute bridge form; do 3 sets of 10-12 reps.

days.title: Upper body
days.work: Learn push-up, band row and overhead press technique; do 3 sets of 10-12 reps.

days.title: Core
days.work: Learn plank, side plank, bird dog and dead bug; hold or repeat for 3 rounds.

days.title: Check
days.work: Demonstrate six exercises with correct form while a parent uses a technique checklist.

objectives: Balance agonist and antagonist exercises
Apply sets, reps and rest for muscular endurance vs. strength

days.title: Endurance vs. strength
days.work: Compare rep ranges and rest periods for endurance and strength; do an endurance circuit (15-20 reps).

days.title: Balance
days.work: Plan a full-body workout that pairs opposing muscles (chest/back, quads/hamstrings).

days.title: Try it
days.work: Complete your designed workout and record sets, reps and perceived exertion.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Adjust exercises that felt too easy or hard using the progression principle.

days.title: Check
days.work: Submit your workout plan with rationale for each exercise.

weeks.topic: Fueling performance: nutrition, hydration and sleep
objectives: Plan pre- and post-exercise snacks
Explain hydration and sleep's role in recovery

days.title: Pre-exercise fuel
days.work: Plan three pre-workout snacks and explain why carbohydrates are the main fuel; do a 30-minute activity.

days.title: Hydration
days.work: Weigh yourself before and after a 30-minute workout to estimate sweat loss and calculate fluid needs.

days.title: Recovery
days.work: Plan a post-workout snack with protein and carbohydrates and explain muscle repair.

days.title: Sleep
days.work: Log sleep for the week and compare to the 8-10 hours recommended for teens; do a yoga cool-down.

days.title: Check
days.work: Create a one-day 'athlete's fuel plan' poster.

weeks.topic: Semester fitness check and plan revision
objectives: Re-check progress on SMART goals
Revise activity plan for semester 2

days.title: Mid-year re-test
days.work: Retest the two fitness items tied to your SMART goals.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Compare results with week 1 and identify whether you progressed, plateaued or declined.

days.title: Overtraining
days.work: Learn signs of overtraining and injury (persistent soreness, fatigue) and how rest prevents them.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise your SMART goals and weekly activity plan for semester 2.

days.title: Active day
days.work: Complete a 40-minute activity of your choice combining cardio and strength.

weeks.assessment: Revised goals and mid-year progress report.

objectives: Perform a golf putt, chip and short swing
Throw backhand and forehand disc golf drives
materials: plastic golf balls or whiffle balls

days.title: Putting
days.work: Practice the putting grip and pendulum stroke to a cup or target from 3, 6 and 9 feet.

days.title: Chipping
days.work: Practice chipping whiffle balls into a hula hoop from 10 and 20 feet.

days.title: Disc drive
days.work: Practice the backhand drive with reach-back and follow-through; measure distances.

days.title: Course
days.work: Set up a 6-hole disc golf or backyard golf course and play a round, keeping score relative to par.

days.title: Analyze
days.work: Explain how angle of release and follow-through affected your distance and accuracy.

objectives: Use a consistent pre-shot routine
Control force for accuracy

days.title: Bocce/bean bag
days.work: Play bocce-style target toss, using underhand toss and controlled force.

days.title: Bowling
days.work: Bowl a playground ball at 10 plastic-bottle pins; learn approach and release.

days.title: Target throw
days.work: Throw at a three-ring target from three distances and record scores.

days.title: Routine
days.work: Design a personal pre-shot routine and compare scores with and without it.

days.title: Check
days.work: Compete in a target-skills triathlon (bowling, bocce, target throw) and record totals.

objectives: Bat and bowl in cricket
Apply fielding strategy

days.title: Cricket intro
days.work: Learn cricket's basic rules and bowl a straight-arm underhand-to-overhand delivery.

days.title: Cricket batting
days.work: Practice defensive and drive strokes to protect the wicket.

days.title: Fielding
days.work: Practice fielding positions and backing up in kickball and cricket.

days.title: Game
days.work: Play a modified cricket or kickball game, rotating batting order.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare strategy in cricket, softball and kickball (striking/fielding games).

objectives: Design an original game with rules and safety
Teach and refine it

days.title: Design
days.work: Design a game combining elements of two game categories (e.g., target + invasion); write rules and scoring.

days.title: Safety
days.work: Add safety rules and equipment checks; draw the playing area.

days.title: Test
days.work: Play-test with family or friends and note problems.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Revise rules based on the play-test and add a modification for younger players.

days.title: Present
days.work: Teach and play the final version; submit the written rules.

weeks.assessment: Written game rules and teaching session.

objectives: Perform basic square dance calls
Use partner etiquette

days.title: Basic calls
days.work: Learn honor your partner, do-si-do, swing and promenade.

days.title: Squares
days.work: Practice a simple square dance with family or a group of four to eight.

days.title: Calling
days.work: Take a turn as caller, giving clear calls on the beat.

days.title: Folk dance
days.work: Learn a Mexican folk dance step (e.g., zapateado basic) or the Virginia reel.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a full square dance; self-assess timing and etiquette.

objectives: Perform swing and salsa basics
Keep rhythm and lead/follow

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Count beats in different songs and clap the tempo; march to 8-counts.

days.title: Swing
days.work: Learn the East Coast swing basic and an underarm turn.

days.title: Salsa
days.work: Learn the salsa basic and cross-body lead.

days.title: Intensity
days.work: Dance 15 minutes continuously and measure heart rate to check if it is MVPA.

days.title: Check
days.work: Perform a 1-minute partner routine combining steps.

objectives: Choreograph a dance-fitness routine
Lead a group through it

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose a song and map out 4 sections of 8-counts with fitness moves (jumps, squats, kicks).

days.title: Choreograph
days.work: Create transitions and formations for a small group.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse and adjust intensity so all participants can join.

days.title: Lead
days.work: Lead family or friends through your dance-fitness routine.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write how dance builds fitness and community; record heart rate during the routine.

objectives: Perform a sun salutation sequence
Explain static vs. PNF stretching

days.title: Sun salutation
days.work: Learn and perform a sun salutation sequence five times.

days.title: Balance poses
days.work: Practice tree, warrior III and chair pose; hold each 30 seconds.

days.title: PNF stretching
days.work: Learn contract-relax PNF hamstring stretching with a strap and measure sit-and-reach before and after.

days.title: Flow
days.work: Create a 15-minute yoga flow of 10 poses.

days.title: Check
days.work: Lead your flow for a family member and record flexibility progress.

weeks.assessment: Yoga flow sequence and flexibility measurement.

objectives: Explain how exercise reduces stress
Use breathing and mindful movement

days.title: Stress and exercise
days.work: Learn how endorphins and reduced cortisol help mood; rate your mood before and after a 20-minute run.

days.title: Breathing
days.work: Practice box breathing and diaphragmatic breathing, then a 10-minute walk.

days.title: Tai chi
days.work: Follow a beginner tai chi sequence for 15 minutes.

days.title: Mindful walk
days.work: Take a 30-minute mindful nature walk, noting five things you see, hear and feel.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a personal stress-relief activity plan with three activities.

objectives: Perform a blind relay baton exchange
Clear low hurdles with correct lead leg

days.work: Practice the upsweep and downsweep handoff while jogging, then at speed.

days.title: Relay
days.work: Run a 4 x 100 m relay (or shuttle relay) with a team, staying in the exchange zone.

days.title: Hurdle drills
days.work: Practice lead-leg and trail-leg drills walking beside low pool-noodle hurdles.

days.title: Hurdle runs
days.work: Run a 3-step rhythm over three low hurdles and time it.

objectives: Perform hop-step-jump sequence
Use the glide or standing put with a soft ball

days.title: Standing put

days.work: Explain how momentum transfers through each phase of the triple jump.

Use even pacing in the 800 m

days.work: Compete in sprint and relay events.

days.title: Meet day 2

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Compare results to goals and grade 7 marks; write a personal-record reflection.

weeks.topic: Lifetime activities: cycling, hiking and swimming safety
objectives: Plan a safe outdoor outing
Identify community recreation options

days.title: Flexibility tests

courses.subject: HEALTH
courses.title: Health Education 8
courses.description: A skills-based grade 8 health course that builds on Health 7 with deeper study of resilience, suicide prevention and the effects of social media on mental health; energy balance, body image and evaluating supplements; comprehensive sexual health aligned with the California Healthy Youth Act (reproduction, abstinence and medically accurate prevention, HIV/STIs, gender identity and respect, healthy relationships and consent, human trafficking and sextortion awareness); opioids, naloxone, addiction and recovery; CPR and violence prevention; and consumer and community health. Sexual health lessons (weeks 11-18) are designed for parent preview, and parents may opt their student out under CA Education Code 51938; an alternative assignment is provided.
courses.framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grades 7–8); 2019 CA Health Education Framework; California Healthy Youth Act (Ed. Code 51930–51939)
